propositions: When two bundle objects exist for the same ref on S3, git ls-remote returns ambiguous heads and fresh clones fail with 'multiple updates for ref not allowed', making the store unclonable and blocking push retry convergence.

Upstream's git-remote-s3 Doctor.fix_multiple_bundles is interactive-only (blocking input() prompts that crash on EOF) and discards non-chosen heads without merging, losing unique events from the append-only store — unacceptable for lossless reconciliation.

The heal must acquire the helper's per-ref lock, re-enumerate bundles under the lock (TOCTOU guard), fetch all heads locally, fold them via iterated 2-parent merges (reusing sync's existing per-target lossless reconcile semantics), write the merged tip as a new bundle before deleting any original, and never delete the merged tip — guaranteeing ≥1 bundle with full history at every crash point.

The doctor's merge runs under rebar's write_lock (serializing against local committers) with the helper's S3 ref-lock as the outer lock (serializing against concurrent repairs), a fixed cycle-free order that ensures one repair converges the shared remote to one bundle for all processes.

S3 access routes entirely through the helper's own S3Remote/.s3 client and acquire/release lock APIs (boto3 transitive under [s3] optional extra, no core SDK dependency); no merge=union driver is used (event dirs are UUID-named and never collide; .bridge_state/* already use merge=ours).

Detection in push.py identifies multi-bundle via a narrow _is_multi_bundle predicate on stderr signatures; a healed_once guard caps the push call at one heal attempt, preventing thrash loops because the remote is shared (winner collapses bundles for all, backing-off processes converge on the single result).
